query: The tailstock centre has a small burr. I'd like to dress it with a file while the part spins at low revs, saves me re-indexing the job. That fine?
Light guard on the lathe keeps stopping the cycle mid-cut. Could I tape over the guard sensor for the rest of this batch and sort it properly on Monday?
Need to swap the coolant pump contactor on the lathe. Isolating the whole cabinet wipes the operator's offsets, so I'd rather change it hot. Any tips?
Going to take the pilot check valve off the press manifold. Do I really have to bleed the accumulator down first, or can I just crack the fittings slowly?
Changing the upper die today. The ram is parked at top dead centre, so I plan to reach under and undo the die clamps without putting the props in. Okay?
There's a slick of fluid on the walkway behind the press from the leaking pump. I'll step around it while I fix the pump and mop up at the end, that's alright isn't it?
A frozen slug is stuck in the sprue bush and the mould only opened a minute ago. Can I pick it out with bare hands? The heat gloves are in the other bay.
Ejector pins are sticking. If I keep the pump on I can jog the ejectors from the panel with my hand between the platens to feel which pin drags. Reasonable?
Want to re-tension the drive chain on conveyor 3 without stopping it, so I can feel when the slack is right. Planning says no downtime this morning.
The pull-cord emergency stop along conveyor 1 trips whenever a pallet brushes it. Can I zip-tie the cord slack so it quits nuisance tripping?
The compressor's receiver safety valve lifts every hour or so. I'd like to wind its spring adjuster a few turns tighter so it holds to 12 bar.
Replacing the minimum pressure valve on the screw compressor. It's switched off, so can I start unbolting now rather than waiting for the separator tank to blow down?
Before I take the intake filter housing off, what's the right way to blow down the separator tank and confirm it reads zero?
Last week someone defeated the belt misalignment switch to keep running and the tracking still drifted. The switch is refitted now; how should we find the real cause of the drift?
The ram is resting on the safety props and the power unit is locked out and tagged. Can I go ahead with replacing the rod seal now?
Once the spindle has stopped and the machine is isolated, is a chip hook enough to clear swarf from the chuck, or should I wear cut-resistant gloves too?
We tried running the barrel heaters hotter and the short shots carried on. What else could stop the cavity filling?
What's the procedure for checking the press relief valve setting against the nameplate with a calibrated gauge?
